attempts.name: addpipe16_kogge_stone
attempts.rationale: The current best-reward design ('(16,)') is likely a Sklansky-style full-width prefix adder, which minimizes prefix-cell count but incurs high fan-out at internal nodes, adding buffering delay. A Kogge-Stone parallel-prefix adder has the same logarithmic depth (4 stages for 16 bits) but strictly fan-out-2 prefix nodes, which typically yields lower critical-path delay after synthesis at the cost of some extra area. Since proxy_reward_v0 weights WNS by 10x versus area by 0.001x, even a modest WNS improvement from reduced fan-out should dominate any area increase, potentially pushing past the current best_proxy_reward point.

attempts.name: addpipe16_condsum_tree
attempts.rationale: Default '+' synthesis ((16,) point) is currently the reward leader, and an explicit gate-level Kogge-Stone attempt underperformed it, showing that RTL coding style materially changes how ABC/OpenROAD map and optimize logically-equivalent adders. Instead of re-deriving G/P AND-OR prefix logic, this design builds the sum via a recursive 'conditional-sum' (carry-select) doubling tree: each bit first computes hypothesis sum/carry pairs assuming incoming carry 0 or 1, and successive levels merge adjacent blocks purely with 2:1 multiplexers selecting between precomputed hypothesis results. This has the same theoretical depth (log2(16)=4 levels) as Sklansky/Kogge-Stone but is expressed entirely with simple mux logic rather than AND-OR generate/propagate merges, which may map more favorably onto Nangate45's mux/AOI cells and yield a shorter critical path (higher WNS) than both the default '+' inference and the explicit KS network, at comparable area.

attempts.name: addpipe16_cla4
attempts.rationale: Two prior attempts (Kogge-Stone doubling network, mux-based conditional-sum tree) both underperformed the plain '+' baseline, suggesting that iterative 2-input associative-merge or mux-chain structures interfere with ABC's ability to re-map/optimize compared to letting Yosys's native $add synthesis pick its structure. This candidate instead uses a classical two-level 4-bit-block carry-lookahead adder (CLA4): group generate/propagate signals are computed directly as sum-of-products over 4 bits (not via iterative doubling), block carries C1..C3 are derived with a second small direct SOP expansion, and per-bit carries within each group are computed directly from local p/g and the block carry-in - all as single-level wide Boolean expressions rather than chained 2-input merges or muxes. This gives ABC wide, natural SOP/POS expressions that map efficiently onto complex Nangate45 AOI/OAI cells with fewer sequential logic levels than a doubling network, while avoiding the extra mux logic and structural sequential dependency chains that hurt the conditional-sum design. This is architecturally distinct from both prior attempts and from the ripple/prefix hybrid splits already on the frontier, offering a plausible path to higher WNS at moderate area, or at minimum a new frontier point.

attempts.name: addpipe16_carryselect8_8
attempts.rationale: All three prior explicit gate-level restructurings (Kogge-Stone, mux-based conditional-sum, 4-bit CLA) underperformed the plain '+' baseline, indicating that Yosys/ABC's native '+' synthesis already produces highly-optimized adder mappings that hand-coded gate networks fail to beat. Rather than fighting the tool's own adder inference, this design keeps two independent native '+' operations (an 8-bit lower add and two speculative 8-bit upper adds for cin=0/cin=1) and only adds a single 8-bit mux selected by the lower carry-out. This halves the effective carry-propagation depth seen by the synthesizer (8-bit chains instead of 16-bit) while letting ABC fully optimize each small '+' the way it already does for the winning (16,) baseline, and only adds one mux level of overhead versus the monolithic add. This is a genuinely different strategy (native-adder carry-select rather than hand-built prefix/mux/CLA networks) and is a plausible way to beat the current best WNS at a modest, bounded area cost (roughly one extra 8-bit adder + 8 muxes versus full 16-bit duplication).

attempts.name: addpipe16_carryselect4_tree
attempts.rationale: All four prior hand-built full-width prefix/tree/CLA/8-8-split adders underperformed the plain '+' baseline, suggesting ABC maps a native 16-bit '+' very efficiently and that deep bit-level restructuring or wide flat mux-chains hurts. This design instead builds a genuine hierarchical (radix-4) carry-select adder: four independent 4-bit blocks are each added twice via native '+' (assuming cin=0 and cin=1, fully parallel, no cross dependency), then combined with only TWO levels of small 4-bit-wide selects (4+4 -> 8, then 8+8 -> 16) instead of four bit-level merge stages (Kogge-Stone) or four levels of 1-bit hypothesis muxes (prior conditional-sum attempt). Using native '+' for the small 4-bit leaves lets Yosys/ABC apply its favorable $add technology mapping at the block level, while the shallow 2-level select tree should give a shorter critical path than a monolithic 16-bit ripple/CLA chain and than the previously-tried flat 8/8 carry-select (whose single big 8-bit adders and single mux level scored below baseline). This is a structurally new point (fine leaf granularity + genuine binary merge tree) not yet attempted, offering a plausible path to a new WNS/area trade-off.

attempts.name: addpipe16_flat_cla_sop
attempts.rationale: All prior hand-built hierarchical adders (bit-level Kogge-Stone, mux-based conditional-sum, block CLA4, carry-select variants) imposed artificial RTL-level structural boundaries (block G/P merges, mux trees, generate hierarchies) and every one of them underperformed the plain native '+' baseline, even though they are logically equivalent. This suggests that imposed hierarchy/boundaries in the RTL are preventing ABC's resynthesis (balance/resub/rewrite) from reaching the same optimum that native $add mapping reaches. This candidate instead expresses the entire 16-bit carry-lookahead as a single flat, fully-expanded sum-of-products for every carry bit (c[i] = OR_j (g[j] & AND_{k=j+1..i} p[k])), with no intermediate named hierarchical block-carry signals and no iterative doubling structure imposed. This gives Yosys/ABC maximum freedom to structurally hash, share, and re-balance the whole carry network from scratch, which for a circuit this small (16-bit adder) is well within ABC's resynthesis capability, and may let it discover a mapping as good as (or closer to) the native-inferred one rather than being locked into a suboptimal user-imposed topology, unlike all previous attempts.

attempts.name: addpipe16_sklansky
attempts.rationale: Six prior hand-built adders (Kogge-Stone, conditional-sum, CLA4, two carry-select variants, flat-SOP CLA) all underperformed the plain-'+' baseline, but none has tried a genuine Sklansky-style prefix tree, which differs structurally from Kogge-Stone: instead of updating nearly every bit at every stage with a variable-distance neighbor (49 merge cells total for KS), Sklansky only updates the upper half of each doubling block, merging it with the single boundary result of the lower half (32 merge cells total, ~35% fewer prefix cells than KS at the same log2(16)=4-stage depth). This trades higher fan-out at the final stage's boundary source for substantially reduced total prefix-cell area, which the previous KS attempt (359.366 area, 7.55092 WNS) suggests is close to competitive already; the extra fanout typically gets buffered efficiently by OpenROAD's placer/CTS-like optimization since it appears only once per stage rather than pervasively. This is a structurally distinct point from all six previous attempts and could plausibly land at lower area with comparable WNS to (16,), improving proxy_reward_v0 or establishing a new non-dominated frontier point.

attempts.name: addpipe16_han_carlson
attempts.rationale: All seven prior hand-built full-width prefix/CLA/select adders underperformed the plain '+' baseline, but none has tried the Han-Carlson topology, which is structurally distinct from both Kogge-Stone (dense fan-out-2 merges on every bit) and Sklansky (upper-half merges every stage). Han-Carlson first pre-merges odd bits with their even neighbor, then runs the deep O(log2(n)) parallel-prefix network only on the 8 odd-indexed lanes (roughly half the prefix cells of Kogge-Stone), and finally does one cheap OR-merge per even bit using the adjacent odd lane's final carry. This should cut total prefix-cell count well below KS (which scored 359.366 area / 7.55092 WNS) while adding only one extra logic level versus Sklansky's fastest-known hand-built variant (319.2 area / 7.49365 WNS), plausibly landing at a new non-dominated area/WNS point between these two previously observed results, and is a genuinely new topology not yet tested in this search.

attempts.name: addpipe16_brent_kung
attempts.rationale: All previous hand-built full-width prefix networks (Kogge-Stone, Sklansky, Han-Carlson) update prefix info at every bit position each stage or every-other stage, giving very wide fan-out cell counts (Sklansky ~32, Kogge-Stone ~49). Brent-Kung is a genuinely different topology not yet tried here: an up-sweep tree that computes full prefixes at only log2(n) touch-points (positions 1,3,7,15 for 16 bits, 15 cells total) followed by a down-sweep that fills in the remaining bit positions with one cheap combine each (11 cells), for only 26 total prefix cells versus 32 (Sklansky) or 49 (Kogge-Stone). This should reduce total gate/area footprint noticeably below Sklansky and possibly below Han-Carlson's 305.9 area, at the cost of a longer critical path (7 logic levels vs 4-5), landing at a new area/WNS trade-off point that may be non-dominated relative to the current frontier (e.g. lower area than Han-Carlson at a still-competitive WNS, or filling the gap between ripple6_prefix10 and addpipe16_han_carlson).

attempts.name: addpipe16_carry_skip4
attempts.rationale: Every hand-built parallel-prefix/CLA/carry-select variant tried so far computes ALL internal carries via wide flat SOP or iterative doubling, and each one landed below the plain native '+' baseline in WNS/reward while incurring extra area from wide AND-OR gates. This candidate tries a genuinely different structural class: a classic carry-skip adder (4 groups of 4 bits). Within each 4-bit group, carries are computed with a plain short ripple chain (cheap 2-input gates, like the area-optimal ripple16 baseline), decoupling group-to-group carry propagation from the intra-group ripple by computing each group's carry-out directly as G_k | (P_k & Cin_k) -- a single OR-AND 'skip' stage fed by pre-computed (Cin-independent) group generate/propagate signals. This turns the 16-bit worst-case ripple chain (~15 sequential FA stages) into ~3 skip hops plus one 3-stage intra-group ripple tail (~6-7 stages), while keeping area much closer to ripple16 than to the flat-SOP/CLA/prefix designs (no wide multi-term AND-OR merge networks beyond simple 4-input group G/P terms). This should land as a new non-dominated point: notably better WNS than ripple16 at much lower area than the ripple_prefix/select hybrids already on the frontier, plausibly improving the area/WNS Pareto frontier even if it does not beat the absolute best proxy_reward.

attempts.name: addpipe16_carry_skip_var
attempts.rationale: All uniform-group carry-skip/CLA/prefix attempts trade cell count for critical-path depth, but analysis of the carry-skip topology shows only the FIRST group's generate delay (feeds into the skip chain) and the LAST group's internal ripple depth (after receiving the final skip carry) lie on the true critical path; middle groups' internal generate/propagate logic is computed in parallel with the inter-group skip chain and is largely off the critical path. The previously-tried uniform 4x4 carry-skip (299.516 area, 7.37783 WNS) wastes delay with a 4-bit ripple tail. This candidate keeps the same 3-hop skip-chain structure (so area/hop overhead stays similar) but rebalances group sizes to [5,5,4,2] bits from LSB to MSB, shrinking the tail group to 2 bits to minimize the final ripple depth while absorbing the extra bits into non-critical middle groups. This should shorten the worst-case combinational path relative to the uniform carry-skip4 point (better WNS) at a similar or only modestly larger area, plausibly producing a new non-dominated area/WNS frontier point between carry_skip4 and the deeper prefix-tree designs.

attempts.name: addpipe16_ripple2_sklansky14
attempts.rationale: The externally observed frontier point ripple2_prefix14 (334.628 area, 7.56156 WNS, reward 75.28) is the closest challenger to the current best (16,) point, clearly beating every full-width hand-built prefix tree this agent has tried (best full Sklansky: 74.62, full KS: 75.15). My earlier ripple3_sklansky13 attempt used the same 'ripple prefix then post-tree carry-merge' structure but at a 3/13 split and scored 74.5 (worse), while the 'fold carry into base G0' variant (ripple4_prefix12_fixedcin) was much worse (71.88), showing that structure choice matters strongly and post-tree merge (not base-fold) is the right family. This candidate keeps the validated post-tree-merge Sklansky structure but matches the empirically best-known split point exactly (2-bit ripple + 14-bit Sklansky), which should land closer to the observed 75.28 reward than my 3/13 attempt, and is a genuinely new split point I have not yet implemented myself.

attempts.name: addpipe16_ripple1_sklansky15
attempts.rationale: The two best-scoring hybrid variants in this search family are ripple2/sklansky14 (75.39 reward, current best) and ripple3/sklansky13 (74.50 reward), showing reward increases as the ripple prefix shrinks toward the tree. This candidate extends that trend one step further: only bit 0 is treated as 'ripple' (c0 = g0[0], which requires zero extra logic beyond the base generate signal, since Cin=0 already makes c0 trivial), and a 15-bit Sklansky tree (still only 4 stages, since 2^4=16 covers 15 elements) computes local prefixes over bits 1..15 assuming local Cin=0, with a single post-tree merge injecting the real carry c0 exactly as in the proven-best ripple2 structure. This removes the one small ripple merge gate that ripple2 needed (g0[1]|(p0[1]&c0)) without adding any tree stages, so it should be at least as fast and potentially smaller than the current best point, testing the next logical split in the winning family.
